title: Tears of the Kingdom Best Early Armor and Upgrades
description: The best early Tears of the Kingdom armor to prioritize, plus how Great Fairy upgrades work and which pieces are worth improving first.
body:
Tears of the Kingdom gives Link access to a huge wardrobe, but the early game does not require you to chase rare armor sets across the entire map. A few accessible pieces can cover the problems that matter most at the start: basic defense, cold protection, stealth and movement utility.

The bigger lesson is that armor becomes much more valuable once you unlock Great Fairy upgrades. Instead of constantly replacing what you wear, build a small practical collection, upgrade the pieces you use most, and keep enough monster parts and materials on hand to improve them later.

For broader early-game guidance, start with our [Tears of the Kingdom beginner’s guide](/stories/tears-of-the-kingdom-beginners-guide/) and see our [Tears of the Kingdom review](/stories/the-legend-of-zelda-tears-of-the-kingdom-review/) for the wider game.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Link overlooks Hyrule in The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, with floating sky islands visible above the landscape.
imageCredit: Nintendo / The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom official artwork.

contentBlocks.text:
For a new file, the Hylian set is the easiest armor recommendation to make because it solves a basic problem without sending you into a dangerous region or a long side quest. Pieces of the set are sold at Lookout Landing, the settlement the main story naturally introduces near the start of the surface journey.

The set does not provide a flashy special effect, but that is part of its value. It gives you dependable defense, works in almost every situation and can be enhanced later. If you are still wearing low-defense tutorial clothing, replacing it with one or two Hylian pieces is an immediate quality-of-life improvement.
contentBlocks.heading: Start With the Hylian Set at Lookout Landing

contentBlocks.text:
Tears of the Kingdom lets you mix head, body and leg pieces freely. Early on, there is no need to spend all your rupees completing a matching set when one useful piece already solves the problem in front of you.

Buy for function first. A stronger chest piece, a cold-resistance item or a stealth piece can be combined with whatever else you own. Full sets become more important later when you are chasing set bonuses, specialized builds or a particular look.
contentBlocks.heading: Do Not Buy a Full Set Just Because It Matches

contentBlocks.text:
The opening Sky Island already teaches that temperature matters, and the surface expands that idea across several regions. One piece of cold-resistant armor can reduce how often you need to rely on temporary food effects when traveling through colder areas.

The Archaic Warm Greaves are a useful early example if you picked them up during the opening, while the Snowquill set in Rito Village becomes a stronger long-term option for players spending time in Hebra. You do not need the full Snowquill set immediately; buying only the protection you currently need keeps early spending under control.
contentBlocks.heading: Keep Cold Protection Available Early

contentBlocks.text:
Stealth-focused armor is valuable because it changes how easily you can approach wildlife, gather insects and avoid drawing attention while exploring. That makes it useful even when its raw defense is not your highest available option.

If your playstyle involves collecting materials, approaching animals or moving carefully through enemy-controlled spaces, carrying a stealth piece can save time in ways a slightly stronger defensive item cannot.
contentBlocks.heading: Stealth Armor Is Utility, Not Just Defense

contentBlocks.text:
Armor enhancement is one of the biggest early progression upgrades available. Nintendo’s own beginner guidance points players to the Lucky Clover Gazette in Hebra to begin Potential Princess Sightings, then to Woodland Stable for Serenade to a Great Fairy. Completing that chain opens your first Great Fairy upgrade access.

Once enhancement is available, ordinary armor can become much stronger. That makes improving a useful piece you already own a better investment than repeatedly buying replacements with similar base defense.
contentBlocks.heading: Unlock a Great Fairy Before Chasing Expensive Armor

contentBlocks.text:
Great Fairy upgrades cost rupees and materials, so spreading resources across every armor piece is inefficient early on. Start with the items that appear in your normal exploration loadout: a general-defense piece, a climate item you use often and any utility armor that supports your preferred playstyle.

This approach keeps your materials concentrated where they have an immediate effect while leaving room to build specialized sets later.
contentBlocks.heading: Upgrade the Pieces You Actually Wear

contentBlocks.text:
It is tempting to sell large stacks of horns, fangs and other monster parts whenever you need rupees. Some of those same materials are used in armor enhancement, which means selling everything can create a second grind later.

You do not need to hoard every item forever, but keep a reserve of common drops until you know which armor you intend to upgrade. Rare materials are especially worth checking before you cash them in.
contentBlocks.heading: Save Common Monster Parts for Enhancement

contentBlocks.text:
The armor screen encourages direct comparison through defense numbers, but defense is only one reason to wear a piece. Temperature resistance, stealth, climbing support, skydiving mobility and other effects can be more important than a few extra points of protection depending on where you are going.

A good early wardrobe therefore looks less like one permanent best set and more like a small toolkit. Carry a dependable defensive option, then swap individual pieces when the environment demands something different.
contentBlocks.heading: Defense and Utility Solve Different Problems

quickRead: The Hylian set is the best simple early purchase because it is available at Lookout Landing, inexpensive compared with specialty sets and easy to keep useful through upgrades.
Unlock Great Fairy enhancement early by starting Potential Princess Sightings at the Lucky Clover Gazette and completing Serenade to a Great Fairy near Woodland Stable.
Keep at least one climate-focused piece such as cold-resistance armor available; utility is often more valuable than a small defense increase.
Do not sell every monster part for rupees. Armor upgrades consume materials, and common drops become useful again as soon as Great Fairy enhancement opens up.
conclusion:
The best early armor strategy in Tears of the Kingdom is simple: buy dependable protection at Lookout Landing, keep one or two useful specialty pieces, and unlock Great Fairy enhancement before spending heavily on replacements.

The Hylian set is a strong foundation because it is accessible and upgradeable, but do not confuse a matching outfit with an optimal loadout. Mix pieces freely, save useful materials, and improve the armor that solves the problems you actually encounter. That approach stays useful much longer than chasing every set as soon as you hear about it.
